string.text: The town bears the grim scars of the Great Plague. Streets are choked with quarantine braziers, citizens wear linen mouth-wraps, and mass graves lie just beyond the walls.
The village struggles in the wake of the pestilence. Smoldering sulfur fires line the perimeter, overgrown weeds choke unworked plots, and surviving kin guard their meager grain stores with scythes.
Dark days... The pestilence took half our kindred, and now ruthless warlords fight over whatever scrap of land is left.
The contagion carried off the best smiths and reapers. The few who survived demand royal silver or took to the hills as bandits.[rf:confused_annoyed]
Wary travels, friend. We burn incense and boil our water at every stop—half the caravans on these roads are carrying the sickness or stripped by plague bandits.
Starving outlaws and plague vagrants lurk beyond the boundary cairns. What good are our taxes if the lord leaves us to fend off desperate survivors alone?
Plague scavengers and desperate deserters prowl the roads outside our gates. The realm fractured, and no captain has come to clear them.
Thank the heavens for {NOTABLE.LINK}. When the fever took our neighbors, {?NOTABLE.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} distributed clean flour and guarded the quarantine line.
They say {NOTABLE.LINK} quarantined three workers from the {.%}{SHOP_TYPE}{.%} the moment they started coughing. Cruel perhaps, but nobody in that quarter has caught the fever yet.
These are dark times. The plague broke all laws—don't worry overmuch about the fate of outlaws.
All right - we give up! Sickness starved our kin and drove us to the road, but we cannot fight soldiers. Show what mercy you can...
You'll never take us alive! Better a clean blade than dying of the black fever in some lord's dungeon![if:convo_angry][ib:aggressive]
So that's how it is, is it? We survived the pestilence; we won't die on our knees! I'll make you bleed before I fall![if:convo_angry][ib:aggressive]
Hold there... You're traveling through our quarantine ground. You don't pass without leaving a toll.
Back off! Dozens of our kin are hidden just beyond that ridge, and every one of us has buried a family and has nothing left to lose.
You don't know who you're dealing with. The woods are full of desperate men who fled the sickness. Step closer and you'll find arrows in your throat.
